subject: Audit slicing and retention options — NovaMed compliance asks
messages:
From: Chris Lang <chris.lang@novamed.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: ComplianceOps <compliance@novamed.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Audit log slicing and retention options

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week — NovaMed's compliance team reviewed the notes and we have a consolidated set of asks to triage before we can proceed to a PILOT. High level: audit granularity, long-term retention for PHI, and BYOK/KMS evidence.

Can you confirm whether Redwood supports per-tenant audit "slicing" (we need CSV-level export where we can filter by tenant_id + time range), and whether audit exports are immutable and time-stamped with requestor identity? Our lawyers require an auditable chain for ePHI access.

Additional specifics:
- Retention options: default 13 months, but NovaMed requires the ability to escrow logs for up to 7 years for subset X (we can provide a mask and list of record_ids).
- BYOK/KMS: we need a handshake proof (timestamped key rotation records) and an encrypted-at-rest proof for exported archives.
- SSO / provisioning: we will need SSO evidence (SAML metadata, assertion logs) tied to the audit stream.

I've attached our compliance questionnaire and a simple audit_scope_matrix.xlsx that maps NovaMed systems to the audit types we need.

Can you route this to the right internal folks and propose a decision path (what's product, what's security, what needs an exception)? A meeting early next week would be ideal.

Regards,
Chris Lang
Director, Compliance
NovaMed Health

Attachments: novamed_compliance_questionnaire.pdf (pdf), audit_scope_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Team — forwarding NovaMed's asks (below). Short summary and triage request:

Summary: client needs per-tenant/exportable audit slices, long-term escrow for PHI up to 7 years, BYOK handshake evidence, and SSO assertion joins to audit stream. They want a clear decision path: product vs. security vs. ops.

Asks:
- Security (Priyom): can we produce key-rotation and KMS-handshake artifacts that satisfy auditor needs? Any gaps?
- Product (Marissa): do we have API/UX to expose export slices and escrow flows, or would this be an exception path?
- Infra (Karthik/Grace): storage + cost implications for 7-year escrow; any retention window constraints and archival mechanics.

Please reply with: 1) short capability status (yes/partially/no), 2) blockers, 3) recommended next step (doc, exception, roadmap). We'll aim to assemble a short decision log to share with NovaMed.

I booked a 30m slot Tue 10:00-10:30 PT — invite pending.

-David

Subject: Re: Fwd: Audit log slicing and retention options — triage request

Quick technical note from Security:

Capability status: PARTIALLY. We already emit a high-fidelity audit stream that includes: requestor_id, tenant_id, timestamps, action, resource_id, and request_headers. Exports can be generated via the /audit/export API but it was designed for operational debugging, not legal escrow.

Gaps / blockers:
- The export API lacks an immutable seal (we do not currently cryptographically sign export bundles). Adding an HMAC/signature on export generation is doable but needs product/operator changes and a review of key usage.
- BYOK handshake artifacts: KMS logs exist but are stored in the control plane; we can expose rotation events, but we will need to define a signed snapshot that ties a rotation event to a specific export (timestamp + export_id).
- Per-tenant slicing: fields exist but there is no UI/templated CSV profile for audit slices. Demand is low today so this is a product ask.

Temporary mitigations:
- We can provide an auditor package (signed statement from Security + exported CSV) as a manual process for pilots.
- For PHI 7yr escrow, propose archived exports stored in a cold bucket with object-level encryption and time-based immutability retention (WORM) — costs and compliance review required.

Needed decisions:
1) Do we add signed export bundles to platform scope (roadmap) or treat long-term escrow as an enterprise add-on + manual process?
2) If roadmap, estimate: ~3 sprints to implement export signing + UI for slice templates; infra work for archived cold buckets adds another 2-3 sprints (depends on procurement of archival storage).

I'll bring a short proposal to the Tue sync.

- Priyom

Product POV:

High level: this maps to two separate deliverables — (A) ad-hoc per-tenant export tooling (low risk, short runway) and (B) an enterprise "escrow" flow with signed export bundles and archival retention (higher risk, cross-team).

Proposed tracks:
- Track A (short): expose templated slices via API + one-click export in Console. Implementation: 2 sprints (engineering + QA). No infra changes if we use existing export path.
- Track B (enterprise): signed export bundles + WORM archival for up to 7 years. Needs: product requirements doc, security design for signing, infra provisioning for cold storage + retention policy enforcement, legal sign-off. Rough estimate: 3-4 quarters for end-to-end (if prioritized).

For the pilot with NovaMed: recommend a hybrid approach — complete Track A for immediate needs and offer Track B as an enterprise add-on (contract + surcharge for archival storage + SLA). We should also scope the manual auditor package as a stop-gap.

Action items for Tue:
- Priyom: bring the minimal spec for export signing and what evidence artifacts look like.
- Karthik/Grace: ballpark S3 Glacier/archival cost for 7 years per TB; can we support WORM?
- David: confirm NovaMed flexibility on contract terms for escrow add-on.

Marissa
Product Lead, Platform

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: ComplianceOps <compliance@novamed.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-22T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit log slicing and retention options — NovaMed next steps

Chris — thanks for the clear asks and the attachments. We've triaged internally and propose the following next steps before the pilot:

1) Short-term (pilot): implement per-tenant templated CSV slices (Track A) and provide a manual auditor package (signed by Security) for exported bundles. No change to your contract required; this will be available for pilot within ~2–3 weeks.

2) Enterprise add-on (optional): develop signed export bundles + WORM archival for multi-year retention (Track B). This will be scoped as an enterprise add-on with pricing and SLA; early estimate points to 3–4 quarters to build end-to-end.

3) For BYOK/KMS evidence: Priyom will surface the exact artifacts we can provide (rotation logs, control-plane events). We will draft a handshake artifact spec and share it in the next 48 hours.

4) Meeting: per the internal invite, Tue 10:00 PT works for our teams — I proposed it and included Novamed; let us know if that conflicts.

Action owners: Priyom (security artifacts + auditor package), Marissa (Track A scope + timeline), Karthik/Grace (archival cost + WORM feasibility). I'll consolidate a short decision log after the meeting and share with you.

Best,
David Kim
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
